subject: Compiler-aligned WVB 1.37 write-pointer lifetime containment
claim: The Windows source-built compiler-aligned verifier accepts exact candidate WVB 1.37 contained write-pointer derivation, enforces an affine two-local move and non-escape boundary, rejects bounded structural and semantic mutations, retains inherited WVB 1.36 admission, and leaves every execution consumer closed.

runs.target: Source-built compiler-aligned WVB verifier deterministic reconstruction
WVB 1.37 write-pointer source, WVIR, byte contract, complete compiler containment, and closed execution boundary

limitations: The focused oracle covered 22 source cases, seven malformed write-region WVIR mutations, seven malformed pointer WVIR mutations, five malformed WVB 1.36 mutations, ten malformed WVB 1.37 mutations, and 25 compiler-verifier decisions; it was not the complete changed-file development plan.

The verifier admits the exact direct borrowed-region parameter and compiler-generated pointer move. It does not yet admit arbitrary pointer control flow, multiple live derived pointers, or a general region-local source.
The scalar provider, native lowerer, launcher, published front door, browser, WebAssembly host, package, and operating-system consumers still reject WVB 1.37.
No provider or native address was formed and no authenticated Foreign call was lowered.

The final verifier source was rebuilt byte-identically through the declared cached split-compiler inputs and packaged successfully; the complete 13-step bootstrap wrapper was not rerun after the last cohesive extraction.
The run is local Windows development evidence and does not claim Linux reproduction, paired-host conformance, qualification, release, or independent reproduction.
